title: An Explainable and Calibrated Multi-Phenotype Diabetes Prediction Framework: Specialized Models, Multi-Dataset Validation, and Longitudinal Assessment

biomarker_validation.description: Biological Endogenous Beta-Cell Function Profile (Nature Sci Data 2023)
biomarker_validation.clinical_conclusion: Fasting C-peptide in T1D cohort exhibits severe beta-cell exhaustion (median 0.016 nmol/L) compared to hyperinsulinemic/insulin-resistant T2D cohort (median 0.410 nmol/L), providing gold-standard biochemical separation alongside EHR feature sets.

harmonized_joint_heldout_evaluation.audit_note: Evaluated strictly on independent held-out partitions with zero sample leakage.

frankfurt_duplicate_audit.scientific_conclusion: Evaluating on Frankfurt Hospital produces artificially inflated generalization metrics (ROC-AUC=0.9482) because 1981 of 2000 rows (99.05%) are duplicates of Pima Indians dataset. This confirms that 'Frankfurt Hospital' is a contaminated re-sampling artifact rather than an independent European clinical cohort.

results.phenotype: Gestational Diabetes Mellitus (GDM) Risk & Early Screening

temporal_leakage_ablation.clinical_significance: Including 24-28 week diagnostic OGTT glucose increases ROC-AUC by +0.0042, empirically demonstrating the magnitude of temporal leakage when diagnostic confirmation is conflated with first-trimester screening. Model 3A establishes the genuine, leak-free early screening benchmark.

speed_classification.task: Rapid Progression (<= 1.5 Years) vs Slower Progression

time_to_event_regression.task: Continuous Years from Prediabetes Diagnosis to T2D

track_4b_cross_sectional_screening.cohort: CDC NHANES ADA Laboratory-Confirmed Cohort (N=1,741 Non-Diabetic Adults)

benchmark.task: Cross-Sectional Non-Glycemic Screening for Undiagnosed Prediabetes (ADA Lab Confirmed)

track_5_mody_monogenic.status: MODEL DEVELOPED AND INDEPENDENTLY VALIDATED (GCK vs HNF1A); ULTRA-RARE SUBTYPES FEASIBILITY DOCUMENTED

results.cohort: Clinical Genetics and Molecular Testing Cohort (N=511)

feasibility_and_rarity_audit.scientific_verdict: GCK-MODY (N=222) and HNF1A-MODY (N=122) possess sufficient sample sizes to support valid 5-fold cross-validated clinical phenotype discrimination (achieving CV ROC-AUC of 0.7385). However, HNF4A-MODY1 (N=4) and HNF1B-MODY5 (N=4) are audited as statistically insufficient for supervised machine learning. In strict accordance with scientific integrity guidelines, we produce a dataset feasibility assessment and clinical literature profile for these ultra-rare subtypes rather than manufacturing an unreliable classifier.

pancreatogenic_type_3c.etiology: Exocrine pancreatic pathology (chronic pancreatitis, pancreatectomy, cystic fibrosis)
pancreatogenic_type_3c.pathophysiology: Simultaneous loss of both insulin-secreting beta-cells and glucagon-secreting alpha-cells, resulting in 'brittle' diabetes with high risk of severe hypoglycemia.
diagnostic_biomarkers: Absence of anti-islet autoantibodies (GAD65, IA-2 negative)
Impaired pancreatic polypeptide (PP) response to mixed meal test
Abnormal pancreatic imaging (calcifications, atrophy on CT/MRI)
pancreatogenic_type_3c.dataset_availability: Extremely limited in public machine learning repositories; no standardized public tabular cohort with confirmed fecal elastase and imaging exists.
pancreatogenic_type_3c.literature_misclassification_rate: 73% to 80% of Type 3c cases are misdiagnosed in hospital records as common Type 2 diabetes.
pancreatogenic_type_3c.modeling_verdict: DATASET INSUFFICIENT — FEASIBILITY DOCUMENTED (Training an ML model on standard EHR targets conflates Type 3c with Type 2 due to diagnostic coding errors).

steroid_induced_diabetes.pathophysiology: Marked increase in hepatic gluconeogenesis and profound peripheral insulin resistance, predominantly manifesting as afternoon and evening postprandial hyperglycemia with normal morning fasting glucose.
steroid_induced_diabetes.diagnostic_challenges: Fasting blood glucose alone frequently misses steroid-induced hyperglycemia; monitoring requires postprandial testing after midday meals.
steroid_induced_diabetes.dataset_availability: Drug encounter records exist (e.g., MIMIC-IV, eICU), but lack structured outpatient taper duration, cumulative dose tracking, and post-steroid normoglycemia resolution data.
steroid_induced_diabetes.modeling_verdict: DATASET INSUFFICIENT — CLINICAL PROFILE DOCUMENTED (Requires dedicated longitudinal pharmacology cohort with cumulative dose tracking).

immune_checkpoint_inhibitor_diabetes.pathophysiology: Fulminant autoimmune beta-cell destruction presenting with rapid progression to diabetic ketoacidosis, often within weeks of therapy initiation.
immune_checkpoint_inhibitor_diabetes.dataset_availability: Rare event incidence (~0.5% to 1.5% of treated oncology patients); published data restricted to single-center case series.
immune_checkpoint_inhibitor_diabetes.modeling_verdict: DATASET INSUFFICIENT — CLINICAL PROFILE DOCUMENTED (Prevalence too low for standard tabular ML training without international multi-center registry access).

icd_9_representation.clinical_limitation: Historically, secondary diabetes codes were rarely applied by admitting physicians unless endocrinology consultation was explicitly obtained.

icd_10_representation.code_family: E08 (Diabetes due to underlying condition), E09 (Drug or chemical induced), E13 (Other specified diabetes)
icd_10_representation.clinical_limitation: Adoption remains inconsistent; many patients are assigned E11 (Type 2 diabetes) out of clinical habit or billing convenience.

results.scientific_conclusion: Secondary diabetes forms (pancreatogenic Type 3c, steroid-induced, endocrinopathy-related) represent critically important clinical conditions that require distinct diagnostic and therapeutic strategies. However, due to documented 75%+ clinical misclassification rates in routine EHRs, absence of exocrine biomarkers (fecal elastase), and negligible representation in public repositories, training an automated machine learning classifier on existing open datasets would produce misleading metrics. In accordance with strict research integrity rules, we document clinical diagnostic criteria, coding pitfalls, and dataset feasibility rather than manufacturing an unvalidated model.
